Net Income vs Reported Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: AEP's reported FCF is structurally negative by design: capital expenditure on the $100bn rate-base build exceeds operating cash flow in every year shown. The DCF values AEP as a dividend-at-cost-of-equity stream instead of owner FCF -- see the DCF section below.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: FCF has been negative every year FY2021-FY2025 and is expected to stay negative through the $100bn, 2026-2031 capital plan -- this is normal for a regulated utility mid rate-base build, not a warning sign. The DCF therefore does not value AEP on owner FCF; it discounts the dividend stream to common at AEP's cost of equity and exits on a year-10 earnings multiple. Net income is the metric that tracks AEP's actual earnings power here.

What to watch:

  • Net income and EPS growth versus the 9-11% guided algorithm, not FCF
  • Whether rising capex is funded by debt/equity issuance on terms consistent with guidance, since FCF will not self-fund it

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentEarnings.title: Segment earnings mix
segmentEarnings.content:
AEP is a holding company of regulated utility subsidiaries; this chart splits net income across the four reporting segments plus Corporate & Other.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: Vertically Integrated Utilities (VIU, cost-of-service states) and Transmission & Distribution Utilities (wires-only, e.g. AEP Ohio, AEP Texas) together are the bulk of earnings; AEP Transmission Holdco is the smallest but fastest-growing segment as transmission rate base roughly doubles to ~$70bn by 2031; Generation & Marketing is the more variable, less-regulated piece. Corporate & Other is usually a drag (parent financing costs, unallocated items).

What to watch:

  • Transmission Holdco's share rising as the $100bn five-year capex plan shifts spend toward transmission
  • Generation & Marketing swings from wholesale power prices, not the rate-base earnings model
  • Corporate & Other getting more negative as debt funds the capex buildout

viuSalesMix.title: VIU sales by customer class
viuSalesMix.content:
GWh of retail electricity sold by AEP's Vertically Integrated Utilities segment, split by residential, commercial, industrial and wholesale customers.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: AEP's regulated earnings are driven by allowed returns on rate base, not by sales volume -- but the customer mix still matters because large industrial and wholesale load (including the contracted data-center pipeline, 84 GW by 2031) is where near-term demand growth is concentrated, while residential/commercial volumes are comparatively flat. A rising industrial/wholesale share corroborates the data-center growth story management cites; it does not by itself raise earnings the way a merchant generator's volumes would.

What to watch:

  • Industrial and wholesale GWh growing faster than residential/commercial (the large-load thesis)
  • Weather-driven swings in residential volumes that are not the structural story

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For American Electric Power Company, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
